summary: Belarus’s conservation pledge is to increase forest cover from 39.9% in 2019 to 41% by 2035, a 1.1-percentage-point rise; the passage also notes a 4.3-percentage-point increase since 1990. The supplied 2022 context records forest at 43.5% of national area, while the pledge uses 39.9% as its 2019 baseline and 41% as its 2035 goal. The mixed (Both) pledge combines restoration and conservation, committing to rehabilitate at least 10,000 hectares of degraded peatlands and bogs, with the period beginning in 2015; the truncated excerpt gives no end date. This minimum area is roughly 32.1% of the mapped wetland class (312 km²). Agriculture covers 53.2% of the country, but no numerical agriculture target appears in the supplied passages.
